text:
Predicates:
RegisterToVote(x, y) ::: x can register to vote in y.
Participate(x, y) ::: x can participate in the election in y.
Citizenship(x, y) ::: x has citizenship of y.
Official(x, y) ::: x is an official of y.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
Premises:
∀x (RegisterToVote(x, unitedStates) → Participate(x, unitedStates2024)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the 2024 United States presidential election.
∀x (Citizenship(x, unitedStates) → RegisterToVote(x, unitedStates)) ::: If someone has United States citizenship, then they can register to vote in the United States.
∀x (Citizenship(x, unitedStates) ⊕ Citizenship(x, taiwan)) ::: A person either has United States citizenship or Taiwanese citizenship.
¬∃x (Official(x, russianFederation) ∧ Citizenship(x, taiwan)) ::: No Russian Federation officials hold Taiwanese citizenship.
¬(Citizenship(vladimir, taiwan) ∨ Manager(vladimir, gazprom)) ::: Vladimir neither holds Taiwanese citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
RegisterToVote(ekaterina, unitedStates) ⊕ Official(ekaterina, russianFederation) ::: Ekaterina can register to vote in the United States, or she is a Russian Federation official.
Conclusion:
¬Official(vladimir, russianFederation) ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official.
